Furthermore, we use the Sobolev embedding $V\hookrightarrow L^p(\Omega)$ with $p\in[2,\infty)$ if $d=2$ and $p\in[2,6]$ if $d=3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The sufficiency claim is false for admissible p other than 6. In (eq:DF-ql) the mixed terms 'integral of (partial_s A delta u) dot grad v' and 'integral of (partial_p B dot grad(delta u)) v' pair a coefficient with delta u (resp. v) in L^p and a gradient factor in L^2, so Hoelder forces the coefficient into L^q with 1/q = 1 - 1/p - 1/2, i.e. q = 2p/(p-2). This strictly exceeds p/2 for every p < 6 (the two coincide only at p = 6). Under the stated assumptions (e.g. d = 3, p = 4, partial_s A in L^2 but not L^4) the bilinear form is unbounded on V x V, so D F(w) need not lie in L(V,V*) and the Frechet-derivative formula is not justified. The exponent p/(p-2) stated for partial_s B is correct; the two p/2 exponents are not.

failure_location.quote: so that all terms in \eqref{eq:DF-ql} are controlled by H\"older's inequality together with the Sobolev embedding for a fixed admissible $p$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exponents L^{p/2} by L^{2p/(p-2)} for partial_s A and partial_p B (equivalently, restrict the sufficiency claim to p = 6) and adjust the accompanying Hoelder bookkeeping; all subsequent content is unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient conditions guaranteeing that the quasilinear model class of Section 2.2 has a well-defined derivative D F(w) in L(V,V*) are incorrect as stated for p in (2,6); the well-posedness of the quasilinear setup is unproven under these hypotheses. No later result invokes these specific exponents (the quasilinear (C3) example uses its own assumptions; the semilinear route is separate), so the damage is confined to this sufficiency claim.
issues.title: Insufficient integrability exponents in the sufficient assumptions for the quasilinear linearisation
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local exponent correction that strengthens two coefficient-integrability hypotheses; no downstream theorem, guarantee, rate, or advertised scope depends on the erroneous exponents, so every substantive claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: For V = H_0^1(Omega) with d in {2,3} (the standing setting of Section 2.1), the embedding V into L^infinity fails: unbounded H^1 functions exist in d >= 2, so no finite C_infinity with ||v||_{L^infinity} <= C_infinity ||v||_V exists, and sup over B_rho of ||w||_{L^infinity} is infinite because the H_0^1-ball contains unbounded functions. Both hypotheses of the example are unsatisfiable in the paper's dimensions, so the conclusion that the u-dependent diffusion model satisfies (C3) on B_rho is vacuous. The gap is structural: the terms pairing the coefficient difference with grad(delta u) dot grad v, and (partial_s a grad w - partial_s a grad z) with delta u dot grad v, involve an arbitrary direction delta u in V against products of L^2 gradients, which forces L^infinity control of delta u and of w - z; within the Sobolev range (p <= 6 in d = 3, p < infinity in d = 2) no Hoelder estimate replaces it. Hence (C3) for the u-dependent principal part cannot be established in the H_0^1 topology in d >= 2 by any variant of this argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: p(\rho):=\eta + \frac{L(\rho)}{2\alpha}\rho^{2}-\rho,
There exists a (computable) nondecreasing function $L:(0,\bar\rho]\to(0,\infty)$ such that for every $0<\rho\le \bar\rho$ and all $w,z\in B_\rho$,
Set $\rho_{\rm up}\gets 2\eta$.
If the quick test fails, bracket an admissible radius by testing a geometric sequence (e.g.,  $\rho_j=2^{-j}\rho_0$) until $p(\rho_j)\leq 0$ and $q(\rho_j)<1$ hold.

issues.failure_explanation: After the initial test at rho = 2 eta fails, the shrinking loop evaluates only candidates rho_low = 2 eta / 2^j <= eta. But p(rho) = eta + L(rho) rho^2/(2 alpha) - rho satisfies p(rho) >= (eta - rho) + L(rho) rho^2/(2 alpha) > 0 for every rho in (0, eta] (L > 0 by (C3); at rho = eta, p(eta) = L(eta) eta^2/(2 alpha) > 0), so no tested candidate can ever be admissible and the loop necessarily exhausts and returns fail. Moreover p(2 eta) = eta (q(2 eta) - 1), so the initial test fails exactly when q(2 eta) >= 1; since q is nondecreasing (affine L), no rho >= 2 eta is admissible either. Hence whenever the quick test fails, all admissible radii (if any exist) lie in (eta, 2 eta) -- the one region the algorithm never probes. Concrete instance (alpha = 1, eta = 0.1, L(rho) = 4 + 5 rho): rho = 0.18 is admissible (p(0.18) = -0.0006 <= 0, q(0.18) = 0.882 < 1), yet the algorithm tests 0.2 (q = 1, fails), then 0.1, 0.05, ... (all with p > 0) and returns fail. Consequently the bisection phase is unreachable dead code, the 'nearly maximal admissible radius' is never computed, and the bracketing-bisection strategy advertised in Remark rem:rho-choice and in the abstract is not delivered.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redesign the shrinking phase to search inside (eta, 2 eta), e.g. locate the minimiser of the convex p by bisection on the monotone p', test admissibility there, then bisect for the smaller root rho_- between eta and the minimiser (or test a geometric sequence c*eta with c in (1,2)); adapt Proposition prop:alg-rho-correct to the corrected search.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:rho returns fail even when admissible radii exist (they can then only lie in (eta, 2 eta), which is never probed); the bracketing and bisection phases can never execute, so the advertised 'nearly maximal' radius selection and the strategy of Remark rem:rho-choice(ii)-(iii) and the abstract are not delivered. The reported experiments are unaffected because the quick test at 2 eta succeeded there (the tables report rho = 2 eta).
issues.title: Radius-selection algorithm probes only provably inadmissible candidates (rho at most eta)
issues.why_classification: The repair requires redesigning the search strategy and re-proving its correctness (a contained but non-routine new argument), so it is more than minor; no global architecture change or loss of a substantive result is needed -- the NK framework, constants, and guarantees are unchanged -- so it is not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \{\rho>0:\ p(\rho) \leq 0\}=[\rho_-,\rho_+] \quad \text{for some $0<\rho_-\le\rho_+$}.
\mathsf{Adm}(\rho)\ \text{fails for all }\rho\in[\rho_*,\rho_{\rm up}],
Because $\mathcal{AD}=[\rho_-,\rho_+)$, admissibility holds exactly on $[\rho_-,\rho_+)$ and fails for $\rho\ge\rho_+$.

issues.failure_explanation: The sublevel set {rho > 0 : p(rho) <= 0} = [rho_-, rho_+] is closed (p(rho_+) = 0), so its intersection with (0, rho_q) equals [rho_-, rho_+], not [rho_-, rho_+), whenever rho_q > rho_+. In that case rho_+ = sup of the admissible set is itself admissible (from p(rho_+) = 0 one gets q(rho_+) = 2(1 - eta/rho_+) < 1 exactly when rho_+ < 2 eta), so the lemma's conclusions that the admissible set 'is either empty or an interval of the form [rho_-, rho_+)' and that Adm 'fails for all rho in [rho_*, rho_up]' (with rho_* = rho_+) are false at the endpoint, and the asserted uniqueness of the threshold rho_* fails (any rho_* in (rho_+, rho_up] then satisfies the two stated conditions). The closed case is realizable: with alpha = 1, eta = 0.1, L(rho) = 4.701 + 1.5 rho one obtains rho_+ of about 0.1993 with q(rho_+) of about 0.997 < 1 and rho_q of about 0.2000 > rho_+, i.e. a closed admissible set. Proposition prop:alg-rho-correct quotes the false 'fails for rho >= rho_+' claim, but its case analysis and conclusions survive the endpoint correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a case distinction in Lemma lem:adm-interval: the admissible set is [rho_-, min{rho_+, rho_q}) if rho_q <= rho_+ and the closed interval [rho_-, rho_+] if rho_q > rho_+; restate the threshold claim accordingly and note that bisection still localises the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:adm-interval mischaracterises the admissible set whenever rho_q > rho_+ (it is then closed and admissible at the threshold); the 'unique threshold' and 'fails on [rho_*, rho_up]' claims are false at that endpoint. Proposition prop:alg-rho-correct's proof invokes this structure and is repaired by the same fix; its stated conclusions remain correct, and the bisection logic is unaffected.
issues.title: Admissible-radius set mischaracterised at the closed endpoint
issues.why_classification: A local case distinction repairs the lemma's statement and proof; the dependent proposition's conclusions are unaffected and no guarantee is lost.
